brief: Soft NFP (lighter payrolls, higher unemployment, better participation) eases near-term Fed pressure and drives curve steepening, though not a genuine bull steepener since the back end had already sold off and the curve still is not rallying; a steeper curve can coexist with a supportive Fed path if growth and earnings stay strong. Energy risk persists (more tanker strikes) but oil keeps exiting the Gulf, capping the tail, and oil is slightly lower. TSMC's breakout to a new Taiwan high is read as an AI-complex signal ahead of its September sales print and Samsung's preliminary numbers, both due Thursday; Nvidia-backed Reflection AI is near an open-weight model release. In Europe, EUR weakens on Spain snap-election risk and France's bigger fiscal problem, with OAT/Bund spreads widening; the week's question is whether an alternative French candidate offers a credible fiscal path. Sentiment and positioning are stretched bearish (Fear/Greed in the 30s, GS sentiment -0.7sd, L/S funds cut ~2pts of gross) even as Nasdaq breaks out while over half the Russell sits 20% off highs, read as contrarian-bullish given how light positioning is.
